payload.purpose_context: #849 is the decisive test for the Life Lattice graph layer: three arms answer the same eight questions over a frozen, oracle-backed corpus, scored on correctness and input tokens per correct answer. The corpus, loader, run harness and gate measurements already exist and are frozen; this mission builds the arms on office4, runs the 72-cell primary matrix and the D-YaRN secondary, and delivers a ledger the design lead can grade blind. The result reads directly on whether the typed graph earns or kills #693.
payload.purpose_tldr: Build the three retrieval arms (graph, full-dump, vector-RAG) and run the pre-registered #849 comparison so #692's build direction is decided by measurement, not argument.

options: Me under auto-run, model resident whenever needed, any hour
Me, but only inside windows Kent declares on the bus
Kent starts each session manually; I only build
payload.question: When the 72-cell primary run executes on office4, who starts and resumes it across session limits, and under what resource envelope — may the 80B model stay resident (~51 GiB GTT, GPU saturated) while you are using the machine, or only in windows you declare?

payload.final_answer: A — office4 session under auto-run runs and resumes the matrix from the ledger; model resident whenever a cell needs it, any hour

options: Primary ledger + grading_view + D-YaRN secondary, then hand to the design lead to grade
Primary ledger + grading_view only; D-YaRN is a follow-on mission
Include blind grading and the section 7 verdict inside this mission
payload.question: Where does this mission end? Is it done when the primary 72-cell ledger is complete and the blinded grading_view is exported, with the D-YaRN secondary also run — or does D-YaRN fall to a follow-on, or does grading itself belong inside?

payload.final_answer: A — done at primary 72-cell ledger complete + blinded grading_view with sealed label map + D-YaRN secondary in its own ledger; grading and section 7 verdict stay with the design lead on the bus

options: Retry up to 2 times after a substrate health check, then record error and continue
Record error and continue immediately; a later resume re-attempts error cells
Halt the run on any infrastructure error and post blocked to the bus
payload.question: The most common exception in a multi-hour run: a cell fails for an infrastructure reason (llama-server crash, FalkorDB connection drop, OOM) rather than a model answer. What must the harness do — retry the cell automatically (how many times), record error and move on, or halt the run until an operator looks?

payload.final_answer: A — retry a cell up to 2 times after a substrate health check passes; then record error and continue; the ledger records every attempt

options: Harness refuses to start if any arm module references the oracle path, AND arms execute in a worktree where oracle/ is absent
Static check only: harness scans arm code for the oracle path before the run
Convention plus code review is sufficient
payload.question: The rule that must always hold: no arm may see the hidden oracle. Today that is a convention. Should the run enforce it structurally, and how?

payload.final_answer: A — enforce structurally twice: harness refuses to start if any arm module references the oracle path, AND arms execute from an environment where oracle/ physically does not exist
